notes:
• Fixed - a Linux server looked for its own sound devices once after it started and never again: with none of its own to list, the look round was over at once, before it was kept as under way, and stayed kept so; a sound card from before was forgotten only if that first round saw it. A round over at once is no longer kept (item 329)
• Fixed - updating Mandarin Bridge for Linux or the Raspberry Pi from Settings → Updates always failed, leaving "Try the update again": the Bridge asked GitHub for the release without saying what it was (no User-Agent), and GitHub refuses every such request. It now says it is Mandarin Bridge, and where an update fails, why is said in words ("GitHub answered 503", not the program's own error code) and shown under the Bridge's row, in the app and on the page; the Android app's row gave a Bridge's long name the room and left its button a few letters a line, as the page now does too: the button's words on one line up to half the row, the name wrapping beside it (item 327). A Bridge already installed can't update itself past this: install it again by hand this once
• Fixed - Mandarin Bridge for Linux and the Raspberry Pi sent DSD as DoP to a DAC that Linux offers native DSD (the owner's SMSL SU-1 on DietPi, kernel 6.12): Linux 6.x lists a raw-DSD altset as "Format: SPECIAL DSD_U32_BE", and the Bridge read only the line's first word. It now reads every format the line names, and sends native DSD, up to DSD512 where the DAC takes it (item 325)
• Improved - a Linux server plays no sound device of its own: a USB DAC on the computer Mandarin runs on is played by Mandarin Bridge for Linux, installed beside it, which plays it as a room of its own (native DSD where the kernel offers it, the DAC kept between tracks). The server's own USB output kept dropping the DAC and competed with the Bridge for it. A sound card the server had in Audio Devices is forgotten by itself, and Audio Devices says how to play a DAC there until a Bridge is listed; the image no longer carries the audio engine, and the container needs no --device /dev/snd or --privileged for sound. SQ-tool's recording of a DAC on the server (off its USB bus) goes with it: Mandarin Bridge records what its DAC is fed. A Mac's own sound devices are played as before (item 324)
• New - Mandarin Bridge for Linux and the Raspberry Pi say when a DAC's native DSD is held back by the computer's kernel: Linux's USB audio driver offers a DAC native DSD only where its own list knows the DAC's maker, so any other DAC is given DSD as DoP even where it says it takes DSD natively (as it did over Mandarin Bridge for Android, whose driver reads the DAC itself). The Bridge now reads the DAC's own USB descriptor, and where it says native DSD and the kernel offers none, its page, its log and /dac.json give the one line that has the kernel offer it for that DAC (an snd-usb-audio option in /etc/modprobe.d), to apply and replug (item 323)
• New - Mandarin Bridge (Android, Linux and the Raspberry Pi) is played one continuous stream of PCM over SlimProto: Mandarin decodes each track itself (and upsamples it, or whatever the Bridge's Output asks) and sends the Bridge the samples alone, one track on into the next in the same stream while they are of one rate and depth, so the Bridge only plays what comes and its DAC is never let go between tracks. Where the next track is of another rate or depth (16/44.1 after 24/96), the stream ends with the last sample of the one before and the next begins a stream of its own, given ahead. A DSD track goes as its file, natively or as DoP, as before. Now playing follows the track heard from where the Bridge is in its stream, and the Bridge's screen and notification are told each track as it comes. A seek makes the track again from there, the track after it still following. Squeezelite players are sent each track's file as before (item 322)
• New - a change of rate between two tracks is given half a second of silence at the new rate before the music, so the DAC settles without a click or pop: on Mandarin Bridge (Android, Linux and the Raspberry Pi), on the Android app's USB direct, and on the server's own sound devices. Tracks of the same rate still follow one another with nothing between them (item 322)
• Fixed - a Mandarin Bridge whose app was installed again showed up as another device each time, in Audio Devices and in Settings → Updates (five rows for one FiiO R7), as did its log: a Bridge that connects from the address an earlier one had, now gone, is that Bridge. It keeps the name and settings it had and the earlier one is forgotten, and Settings → Updates lists each Bridge once (item 321)
• New - a device's Output opens with Sound, its settings as recipes: Bit-perfect; where it takes more than 48 kHz, Upsampled with the Standard filter, with the Gaussian ones, with them in minimum phase, and with the Very long filter and shaped dither; where it takes DSD, DSD at its highest multiple with the 7th-order modulator. Each says what it does for that device (its highest rate, its real bits, its DSD rate), the one in use marked; a tap sets what it names and leaves the rest. Custom, or any row changed, opens Advanced, where every row of the Output is as before; DSD as PCM, the player, Gapless and Fixed volume stay outside it (item 320)
• Fixed - the Standard filter's words say again that for PCM it is SoX's filter, Mandarin's own on the way to DSD and in minimum phase (item 320)
• New - Phase on a device's Output, Linear or Minimum, for both its filters: in minimum phase each filter keeps its levels at every frequency and puts all its ringing after a sound (0.15 ms before it at most, where the linear filters ring 0.2 to 47 ms before). Every filter but Gaussian steep, which keeps every sample of the file only in linear phase. The filter list's Minimum phase is now the standard filter with Phase set to Minimum; a device set to it is kept so. The list's notes now say each filter's measured figures (item 318)
• New - two long filters on a device's Output, Long and Very long: the standard filter's design made 8 and 32 times as long (262,145 and 1,048,577 taps at ×16), flat to 21.8 and 21.9 kHz for a CD and 270 and 284 dB down from 22.1 kHz, where the standard filter is flat to 21 kHz and 113 dB down there; their ringing, either side of a sound, 28 and 47 ms where the standard's is 8, at 22 kHz. They run as fast as the standard filter; a track takes 0.15 s and 0.6 s longer to start, and Very long takes some 400 MB while it plays. Mandarin's own, made as the track plays, joined to its album's neighbours as the others are (item 317)
• Fixed - an album's track made DSD on into the next one could wait for ever where the next was shorter than the upsampler holds back (a quarter of a second with the standard filter, seconds with the long ones): its file is now finished from what is in (item 317)
• Improved - upsampling and making DSD take far less of the processor, with the same output: PCM as DSD256 now takes 37% of one core per second of music where it took 68% (DSD128 20% from 41%, DSD64 15% from 28%; measured on a 2.1 GHz Xeon), and upsampling ×16 runs 1.5 times as fast. The filter's transform and the doublings to the DSD rate work four samples at a time, giving the same bits as before; the modulator's sums are taken in an order that waits less between samples (its measured noise unchanged), and one core now runs both channels' modulators, where each took a core (item 319)
• New - where Mandarin makes the PCM (upsampled, not made DSD), a device's Output sets how its last bit is rounded: the DAC's real bits (as sent, or 23 to 20, the bits it resolves above its own noise, the dither put in at that bit and those below left at zero) and the Dither, Flat (the default, as before) or Shaped of the 3rd or 5th order, its noise moved above the audio band. Measured on a tone at half scale at 705.6 kHz and 20 bits: Flat −130 dB in the band, Shaped 3rd −192 dB, Shaped 5th −233 dB, each with more noise above the band. Shaped is made at 88.2 kHz and up; at 44.1 and 48 kHz, Flat. Mandarin's own, made as the track plays; Now playing's signal path says it (item 301)
• New - Mandarin Bridge for Linux and the Raspberry Pi play from Mandarin over SlimProto as the Android one does, where they were UPnP renderers: found by themselves (or pointed at Mandarin with --server), their DAC read as before, its ✓ shown, updated and their logs read from Settings → Updates; their name and settings kept (item 316)
• New - Mandarin Bridge for Android plays from Mandarin over SlimProto, where it was a UPnP renderer: it finds Mandarin by itself, and Mandarin reads its DAC from it as before (its rates, its ✓, its updates and its log in Settings → Updates). Each track Mandarin sends it says what it is, for the Bridge's screen and notification. A Bridge Mandarin knew as a UPnP renderer keeps its name, whether it was on, and its settings. Mandarin Bridge is 0.3.0 (item 315)
• New - a Squeezelite player's page has Output, as a renderer's: upsampling (×2, ×4, Max), the filters, the bit depth, DSD as PCM, PCM as DSD and its modulator; its rates and DSD are its own word, from its hello. Gapless says it plays one track into the next from its own buffer, with nothing to set, and how its -r option pauses at a change of rate. About says it connected to Mandarin, over SlimProto (item 313)
• New - seeking on a Squeezelite player: it can't seek within what it fetches, so the track is fetched again from that point; upsampled or made DSD it is made from there, as an album's stream is begun part-way (item 313)
• Fixed - the ✓ on Now playing for a Mandarin Bridge could never come for a track: Mandarin asks the Bridge what it feeds its DAC once a track has played a couple of seconds, and where that one ask went unanswered, or the Bridge said it played nothing (busy, or between tracks), it never asked again for that track. It now asks again at the next read until it has the Bridge's word (item 314)
• New - Squeezelite players (and Squeezebox-compatible hardware) play from Mandarin over SlimProto: Mandarin answers on port 3483, a player finds it by itself or is pointed at it (squeezelite -s <server-ip>), and appears in Settings → Audio Devices under the name it gives; switched on, it plays the queue one track into the next from its own buffer, never stopping between them, with Pause, Next, Back and the volume. To pause at a change of rate so the DAC settles without a click, start Squeezelite with a rate list and delay (e.g. -r 44100-768000:500). Seeking, and choosing upsampling on a Squeezelite player's page, follow (item 312)
• Fixed - a command the server doesn't have (one typed wrongly, or from a newer Mandarin) started a second server inside the container beside the one running, its jobs and Tailscale with it, until it fell over on the port: it now says there is no such command, lists those there are, and stops (item 310)
• Fixed - upsampling to PCM played nothing on a Chord Poly or a Mandarin Bridge on a FiiO R7: a device whose bit depth was Auto, and which listed 32 bits, was sent 32-bit FLAC, which neither could decode. Auto is now 24 bits; 32 goes out only where a device is set to 32 (item 308)
• New - a device's own player (Settings → Audio Devices → a device → Output → Player): where a renderer has MPD beside it, as a Chord Poly does, Mandarin can hand MPD the queue instead of UPnP, and MPD plays one track into the next by itself, gapless, as it plays its own library; Mandarin follows it from what MPD says (item 306)
• Fixed - Albums as one stream on a Chord Poly went a track at a time, with a long gap at each: the Poly named the track it had been playing for a moment after the album started, and Mandarin took that for the album stream having ended. It now stays one stream (item 305)
• Fixed - PCM at 705.6 and 768 kHz played nothing on a Chord Poly, which can't decode FLAC at those rates: it goes as WAV again, as before. With Albums as one stream at those rates, an album goes as a few streams of under 4 GB each (12.7 minutes at 32-bit/705.6 kHz), the most a WAV can say (item 307)
• New - a choice of three DSD modulators for PCM made DSD (Settings → Audio Devices → a device → Output → Modulator): the 7th order (as before), the 7th order wide, which holds its noise down to 50 kHz (DSD128 and DSD256), and the 9th order, quieter in the audio band (DSD64 and DSD128); each measured and shown with its figures, and the signal path says which one made the track (item 303)
• New - Albums as one stream (Settings → Audio Devices → a device → Output → Gapless): an album's tracks go to the device as one stream, start to end, made in one (upsampled, or made DSD), so it plays gapless however it joins files; Mandarin still shows each track, and a skip or a seek starts the stream again there (item 300)
• Fixed - Mandarin Bridge for Android, and the app's USB direct, let go of the DAC between two tracks and took it again, dropping the last moment of the track before and starting DoP's marker over: a track that goes to the DAC as the one before did now follows on in the same stream, gapless. Mandarin Bridge is 0.2.3 (item 304)
• Fixed - a Chord Poly moving on by itself from one track made DSD to the next: Mandarin stayed on the first track, and near the end of the second started it again from the beginning. Mandarin now follows any device that goes on naming the first track (item 299)
• New - three Gaussian upsampling filters: Gaussian (smooth, very short ringing, the top of a CD a little down), Gaussian steep (flat almost to 22 kHz, every sample of the file kept) and Gaussian hi-res (for 88.2 kHz and up), each made as the track plays, PCM or on the way to DSD (item 298)
• New - each device has a filter for CD-rate sources and one for hi-res sources (or the same): two rows in Settings → Audio Devices → Output, each opening the list of filters with what each does (item 298)
• Fixed - Google Play Protect called Mandarin Bridge for Android harmful: it installed its own updates without asking. Now Update in Settings → Updates puts a notification on the device, whose tap downloads the update in the browser for you to install; Mandarin Bridge is 0.2.2 (item 297)
• Improved - the menu is the first button of the bar along the foot, so it opens from every screen; Home's own menu button is gone (item 296)
• Improved - Now playing keeps the bar along the foot, its cover smaller to make room (item 296)
• Fixed - the favourite heart is a proper heart: both halves alike, one point at the foot (item 296)
• Fixed - the Release workflow tests as CI does: it builds Mandarin Bridge for Linux and installs SQ-tool's numpy before its tests (item 295)
